statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail is 31% in the elevated band and Stress is high at 75%, with the US cash open still pending.
recommendation: Nasdaq-100 futures are at 29,089-29,093, down about 1.42% and 420 points from the 29,513 previous close, after extending the session low for a third consecutive hour to 29,086.50. The prior lows were 29,178.00 and 29,137.50, so each stall has resolved by extension rather than by a reclaim, and price is holding within roughly 7 points of the current low on a session range of 29,086.50-29,571.25. That sequence, rather than the size of the move, is what lifts Tail from 28% to 31%. The cross-asset stack is aligned: the US 10-year is 4.79% and rising for a fifth consecutive session, the 30-year is 5.27% near multi-decade highs, WTI is $88.25 and Brent $92.70 after verified projectile strikes on two crude carriers in the Strait of Hormuz, and VIX is 15.95, up 6.9%, though still low in absolute terms. Semiconductors are the transmission point, with Intel, AMD and NVIDIA all lower pre-market on a rates-driven rather than company-specific move. Tail stays below the strong-block threshold because the extension is an orderly grind of roughly 40-50 points per hour rather than violent repricing, the session has already traded a 485-point range, and the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM/JOLTS block are checkpoints that have not yet printed. Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures extend the session low a third straight hour to 29,086.50 into the cash open, with the 10-year at 4.79% and crude above $88 on Hormuz tanker strikes
body:
The down-leg has now extended in three consecutive clock-hours. Two quote sources place Nasdaq-100 futures at 29,089.25-29,093.25 shortly after 13:16 UTC, about -1.42% and -420 points against the 29,513.00 previous close, with a session range of 29,086.50-29,571.25. The low has moved from 29,178.00 to 29,137.50 to 29,086.50 across the last three hours and price is sitting within roughly 7 points of it. That is the specific pattern the Tail definition is written around: repeated extension after failed retracement, with the instrument holding near its extreme rather than mean-reverting away from it.

The driver is not equity-specific. A global government bond selloff has pushed the Bloomberg global sovereign gauge to its highest yield since mid-2008, with the Japanese 10-year at 3% for the first time since 1996 and the UK 10-year gilt at 5.25%, the highest since 2008. The US 10-year at 4.79% is at its highest since January 2025 and the 2-year is 4.38%. Rate-sensitive long-duration names carry that repricing most directly, which is why semiconductors lead the decline: Intel is down about 3%, AMD and NVIDIA about 2%, and the semiconductor ETF roughly 2% lower pre-market. The Finviz cross-asset context collected at 10:50 UTC, which is delayed latest-session data rather than live price-path evidence, corroborates the tone: all eight tracked megacaps and all seven tracked semiconductor names were negative, with technology the weakest sector at -0.94%.

The energy leg is a separate and unresolved input. Two very large crude carriers, one operated by Saudi Arabia's Bahri and one by Sinokor, were struck by projectiles while exiting the Persian Gulf near Khasab, Oman. WTI is $88.25, up 2.9%, and Brent $92.70. Because the inflation channel connects crude directly back to the rates impulse, the two amplifiers reinforce each other rather than offsetting.

Set against that, several things argue for keeping Tail inside the elevated band rather than escalating further. The extension is orderly, roughly 40-50 points an hour, not a violent one-way repricing. VIX at 15.95 is up sharply in percentage terms but remains low in absolute terms, which is not the volatility signature of a no-retracement regime. The session has already traded a 485-point range, so two-way trade has been available. And the two events that would most plausibly convert this into a lethal path, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC block of ISM Manufacturing, ISM Prices and JOLTS, have not printed yet: neither the opening auction nor the post-release path is observed, and hypothetical alignment is not scored as though it had already happened.

The danger window is therefore drawn narrowly around 13:30-15:30 UTC, covering the opening auction, the 14:00 release block and the first full hour of post-release price discovery. Projected Tail peaks at 34% in the 14:00 UTC hour and then steps down through the afternoon on the base case that price discovery is orderly and retracements return, with a modest lift back for the 19:00 UTC power hour. A fresh session low below 29,086.50, or an opening auction that continues directly with shallow pullbacks, would be the evidence that invalidates that decay path.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The first nineteen, covering the August 31 US session and the overnight hours, mapped to the EA_ON band with Tail between 9 and 13 and mode mixed throughout, while Stress drifted from 52 up to 58 as crude extended and the 10-year climbed after the Jackson Hole address: the backdrop deteriorated but the price path itself stayed two-sided, so Tail stayed compressed. The regime changed in the final five hours. At 08:00 UTC Tail moved to 22 with mode trend-down as the overnight band gave way, then to 26 at 09:00 UTC, the first BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES reading of the sequence. Tail held at 25 through the 10:00 and 11:00 UTC hours while price stalled on a 29,178 base, then rose to 28 at 12:00 UTC when that base broke to 29,137.50. Stress rose in step from 65 to 72 and confidence stayed between 84 and 87 throughout.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is that today's combined rates, crude and geopolitical repricing resolves into two-sided trade rather than a persistent no-retracement path, but the projection now starts from a leg that has extended in three consecutive hours rather than one that is stalling. Tail is 31 for the current 13:00 UTC hour covering the pending cash open and peaks at 34 with Stress at 79 in the 14:00 UTC hour, when ISM Manufacturing, ISM Prices and JOLTS print together 30 minutes into the session, with mode projected event/whipsaw. That peak stays below the strong-block threshold because event dispersion and surprise magnitude are scored as Stress and Confidence until an actual price path is observed. From 15:00 UTC the projection steps Tail down through 32, 29, 27 and 25 on the assumption that post-release discovery is orderly and retracements return, with a one-step lift back to 26 for the 19:00 UTC power hour and its documented late-session continuation tendency. After the 20:00 UTC cash close Tail falls back into the watch band and then the low band overnight, reaching a floor of 14 during the Asian afternoon, before rising again through the European open on the possibility that the global rates impulse re-transmits via bunds and gilts. The final hours lift Tail to 22 for the 12:00 UTC ADP window on September 2. Confidence decays steadily from 88 to 54 across the projection because later hours rest on modelled rather than observed conditions. The decay path is invalidated by a fresh session low below 29,086.50, an opening auction that continues directly with shallow pullbacks, or a further extension in global yields.
